sources.title: Rear Wheel Roll Steering (Passive) Suspension Mechanism
sources.summary: This paper focuses on the concept and ideas for the development of Passive Four-Wheel Steering and will act as a foundation to build a robust and practical design. We always seek new methods to improve over existing ones, steering the rear wheels is always a fascination that an automotive engineer dreams of. The concept of treating angle as a vector quantity and further taking components of it and using them to generate Toe (steer) in the rear wheels through suspension linkages in accordance with the direction of cornering is analyzed in detail. Along with this a virtual design is incorporated and simulated to prove the practicality of the concept.

sources.title: Turning data into pedagogical action : designing the learning analytics cockpit, a teacher dashboard for feedback
sources.summary: Teachers play a central role in our society as they foster the intellectual and personal development of students. One of their core responsibilities is the systematic monitoring of individual learning processes. While observing student performance and deriving targeted interventions are essential competencies, implementing them in everyday classroom practice can be demanding, particularly in large and heterogeneous groups. Learning Analytics (LA) offer new opportunities to support this process by enabling the real-time collection and analysis of learning data. LA systems are increasingly developed to help teachers make informed, data-driven decisions. To facilitate such pedagogical decision-making, teacher dashboards provide visual representations of student learning data. However, their potential to improve teaching and learning remains limited. Many dashboards lack clear actionability, meaning it is often unclear to teachers what specific steps to take to support student learning after viewing the data. Furthermore, teachers are rarely involved in their development, which reduces both acceptance and practical usability. In addition, there is limited empirical evidence demonstrating the actual impact of dashboards on student learning outcomes. This dissertation addresses these challenges by introducing the "LA Cockpit" and conceptualising a teacher dashboard as a feedback tool. It moves beyond mere data visualisation by enabling teachers to provide feedback to students and make interventions directly through the dashboard. The requirements for the LA Cockpit were developed in a co-design process with teachers, grounded in their practical challenges in monitoring learning and providing feedback. The effectiveness of the LA Cockpit was evaluated in a quasi-experimental intervention study conducted in secondary school physics classes. Findings show that students in the intervention group achieved significantly greater learning gains than those in the control group, providing empirical evidence for the educational benefits of a co-designed, feedback-oriented dashboard. This dissertation makes three key contributions: (1) it proposes an expanded conceptualisation of teacher dashboards as tools for feedback, (2) develops a design-oriented framework for their implementation in school contexts, and (3) presents empirical evidence of their effectiveness in authentic classroom settings. Overall, the study lays a foundation for future research on the practical impact of educational technologies, such as teacher dashboards, in schools.

sources.title: Four-wheel-steering Control Strategy and its Integration with Vehicle Dynamics Control and Active Roll Control
sources.summary: <div class="htmlview paragraph">The paper presents a 4-wheel-steering (4WS) control strategy devoted to reduce the turn diameter for small longitudinal speed values and to obtain a yaw rate damping effect in dynamic manoeuvres. Moreover, the 4WS active system conceived produces compensation both for lateral wind and road irregularities. The main results obtained through a functional vehicle model are presented. 4WS was integrated with a Vehicle Dynamics Control (VDC), which was improved for turn while braking manoeuvres. The results due to integration were very good, with a reduction of both systems interventions. Finally, a VDC-4WS-Active Roll Control (ARC) integration was tried, based on only one reference body yaw rate for all the active systems. The main results obtained are presented and discussed.</div>
